title: Classic Slow-Cooker Beef Pot Roast

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck pot roast, trimmed of excess fat

steps: Pat chuck roast dry and season all sides with kosher salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear roast for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply browned on all sides; transfer to slow cooker.
In the same skillet, sauté onions, celery, and garlic for 2 minutes to loosen fond; pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce, bringing to a simmer.
Arrange carrots, potatoes, and herb sprigs around the roast in the slow cooker. Pour warm broth mixture over top.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours (or in 325°F oven for 3 hours) until beef is fork-tender (internal temp 195°F–205°F).
Transfer roast to a cutting board, rest for 10 minutes, and slice or shred into large pieces. Serve with the braised vegetables and rich pan juices.
swaps: Can substitute rump roast or bottom round; red wine can replace 1 cup of beef broth.
notes: Searing first develops rich flavor; cooking low and slow dissolves connective tissue into gelatin.

title: Heart-Healthy Slow-Cooker Beef Stew

ingredients.name: lean beef stew meat (chuck), cut into 1-inch cubes

steps: Toss beef cubes with flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl to coat lightly.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in uncrowded batches (3 to 4 minutes per batch); transfer to slow cooker or stew pot.
Add diced onion, celery, and garlic to skillet, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in tomato paste and 1 cup of beef broth, scraping up browned bits from bottom.
Add potatoes, carrots, remaining broth, thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, and sautéed mixture into pot with beef.
Cover and simmer on low for 6 to 7 hours (or in 325°F oven for 2.5 hours) until beef is meltingly tender and gravy is thickened.
Discard bay leaf, season with additional black pepper, and ladle into warm bowls with crusty bread.
swaps: Can add 8 oz sliced cremini mushrooms; sweet potatoes can replace Yukon golds.
notes: Dusting beef lightly with flour gives meat a rich brown crust and naturally thickens the stew broth.

title: All-American Cast-Iron Hamburger Patties

source.name: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse

steps: Divide ground beef into 4 equal portions (6 oz each). Shape gently into 3/4-inch thick patties, pressing a slight depression in the center with your thumb to keep patties flat during cooking.
Season both sides generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder just before cooking.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until hot. Melt butter to coat the pan.
Add patties to skillet. Cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes until a deep caramelized crust forms.
Flip patties with a spatula. If adding cheese, place cheese slices on top now. Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes without pressing down on patties.
Check with an instant-read thermometer inserted horizontally into center of patty until temperature reads exactly 160°F (medium doneness).
Transfer to toasted buns and serve immediately with favorite toppings.
swaps: Can use ground chuck or ground sirloin; Swiss or pepper jack cheese can substitute for cheddar.
notes: Never press down on patties while searing to preserve natural juiciness. Cook to 160°F for food safety.

title: Oven-Roasted Classic Beef Rib Roast

source.name: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse
source.location: How to Cook Beef Roasts Section

ingredients.name: bone-in beef rib roast (prime rib), fat trimmed to 1/4 inch
coarse sea salt and cracked black pepper
fresh rosemary and thyme, finely chopped

steps: Remove rib roast from refrigerator 1 hour before cooking to bring to room temperature. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Preheat oven to 450°F (232°C).
Mix olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme, coarse salt, and black pepper into an herb paste; rub paste evenly across all surfaces of the roast.
Place roast bone-side down (fat-side up) on a rack inside an open shallow roasting pan.
Roast at 450°F for 15 minutes to establish a crisp browned crust.

Reduce oven temperature to 325°F (163°C) without opening the oven door. Continue roasting for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest part reads 135°F for medium-rare.
Transfer roast to a carving board, tent loosely with aluminum foil, and rest for 15 to 20 minutes (internal temperature will rise to 145°F). Carve between bones and serve.
swaps: Can use boneless strip roast or eye of round roast (adjust cooking time per pound).
notes: Resting 20 minutes is critical to prevent juices from draining onto the carving board.

title: One-Skillet Cheesy Ground Beef and Potatoes

ingredients.name: russet or red potatoes, diced into 1/2-inch cubes

steps: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add diced potatoes and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden-brown and tender; transfer potatoes to a plate.
Add ground beef and diced onion to the skillet. Cook over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking meat into crumbles, until beef is browned and reaches 160°F. Drain excess grease.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, cooking for 1 minute.
Return cooked potatoes to skillet and pour in beef broth, stirring to scrape up any browned bits on pan bottom.
Simmer for 2 minutes until liquid is mostly absorbed.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top. Cover skillet for 2 minutes (or place under broiler) until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve directly from the skillet.
swaps: Can substitute sweet potatoes for russets; ground turkey can be used in place of ground beef.
notes: Comforting one-skillet family dinner combining savory browned beef, crispy potatoes, and melted cheese.

title: Three-Bean and Beef Chili
steps: In a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat, brown ground beef for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until cooked through (160°F). Drain excess fat.
Add chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic to pot, cooking for 4 to 5 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, black beans, kidney beans, and pinto beans, stirring to combine.
Bring chili to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and chili is thick.
Ladle into bowls and serve with optional shredded cheese, sour cream, and warm cornbread.
swaps: Can substitute diced chuck roast for ground beef (simmer for 1.5 hours); can add chipotle in adobo for extra heat.
notes: Three bean varieties provide creamy starch textures while ground beef provides rich savory depth.

title: Panamanian Spiced Beef with Mofongo

ingredients.name: beef chuck or flank, sliced into thin strips
green plantains, peeled and sliced into 1-inch rounds

steps: In a skillet over medium heat, pan-fry plantain rounds in oil until golden on outside and tender inside (approx. 8 minutes); remove to a mortar or bowl.
Mash warm plantains with 2 cloves minced garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, a splash of broth, salt, and pepper into a savory mofongo mash; shape into mounds.
Heat remaining oil in a heavy skillet over high heat. Add beef strips and sear for 3 to 4 minutes until browned.
Add sliced onion, bell pepper, remaining garlic, cumin, and oregano, cooking for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste, beef broth, and lime juice, simmering for 5 minutes until sauce coats the beef.
Plate saucy spiced beef alongside mounds of garlicky plantain mofongo and serve hot.
swaps: Can use yuca (cassava) or mashed potatoes if green plantains are unavailable.
notes: Bold Latin American dinner balancing savory spiced beef strips with garlicky plantain mofongo.
